Perfect! I've updated the cargo check command to use `tee` which will:

1. **Display output in real-time** - You'll still see all the compilation results as they happen
2. **Save to file** - All output (both stdout and stderr) will be saved to `cargo-check-results.log`
3. **Preserve everything** - You won't miss any errors or warnings since they're all captured in the log file

Now when you run the compilation check, you'll get a `cargo-check-results.log` file that contains the complete compilation output, making it easy to review any errors or warnings later without having to re-run the lengthy compilation process.
